title: Sherpa Tensing — Camp Twelve: Future Perfect (B2) | Forbes English
description: Camp ten looks back from a moment in the past. Camp twelve does the same thing facing the other way: it stands at a point in the future and tells you what…

hero.lede: Camp ten looks back from a moment in the past. Camp twelve does the same thing facing the other way: it stands at a point in the future and tells you what is already behind you by the time you arrive.

cards.head: Finished before a future deadline
cards.body: The action is over by the time the future moment arrives.
cards.ex: "By Friday I will have finished the report."

cards.head: With by the time
cards.body: The clause that sets the deadline stays in the present.
cards.ex: "By the time you land, we will have left."

cards.head: A total reached by then
cards.body: Counting up to a future point rather than to now.
cards.ex: "Next month she will have worked here ten years."

cards.head: A confident guess about now
cards.body: Not future at all — an assumption about something already done.

cards.head: Looking back from the future
cards.body: Standing at a future moment and describing what is behind you.

cards.head: Not done by then
cards.body: The negative is just as useful, and just as precise.

cards.head: Wh- questions
cards.body: question word + will + subject + have + participle?

charts.head: Conjugation chart
charts.note: Nothing changes for the subject — will have is the same for everybody, exactly as it is at camp seven. Every difficulty here is in the participle and in the deadline word.

charts.head: By or until?
charts.note: This is the error that costs money in a work email. By Friday means at any point up to and including Friday — a deadline. Until Friday means the whole stretch continuing up to Friday — a duration. The future perfect takes by.

head: Word
Means
Example
rows: at or before that point — a deadline
right up to that point — a duration
a deadline set by another event
"By the time it opens, we will have queued an hour."

charts.head: Three mistakes worth naming
charts.note: Almost every error with this tense is one of these three.

head: Not this
This
Why
rows: By Friday I will finish the report.
By Friday I will have finished the report.
A deadline needs the perfect. Will finish names when it happens, not that it is already done.
I will have went by then.
I will have gone by then.
Have takes the third form, never the past simple.
By the time you will arrive, we will have left.
By the time you arrive, we will have left.
The clause that sets the deadline stays in the present, even though it is about the future.

charts.note: Camp seven says when something happens. Camp twelve says it is already done by a point you name. If there is a deadline in the sentence, you are at camp twelve.

head: Question
Future perfect
Future simple
rows:
It is finished before then.
"I will have finished by five."

It happens at that time.
"I will finish at five."
Yes. "She will have worked here ten years."
Yes, as a confident guess: "He will have landed by now."
No. That is a different job.

charts.example: The pair that shows the whole difference: "I will finish at five" — five o'clock is when I stop. "I will have finished by five" — five o'clock is when you can safely assume it is done, and I may well be finished long before. One is a schedule; the other is a promise.

sections.example: A useful habit: if you can put the word already in front of the verb and the sentence still makes sense at that future moment, the future perfect is right.

diagram.intro: The block is the action, standing in future time. What matters is that it ends before the dashed line, not on it — the deadline is a moment you look back from, not a moment when anything happens. The action itself could be at any point in the shaded stretch; the sentence only promises it is behind you by then. Click the block or the NOW column to see it in a sentence.

panels.head: Future perfect — already behind you
items: By Friday I will have finished the report.
We will have left before you land.
She will have worked here ten years.

panels.head: The deadline clause — it stays present

quiz.hint: There is a deadline in the sentence.
quiz.explain: By + a future point needs the perfect: it says the report is already done when Friday arrives.

quiz.prompt: By the time you land, we _____ . (leave)
quiz.hint: One future event sets the deadline for another.
quiz.explain: By the time sets a deadline, so the main clause takes the future perfect. The participle of leave is left.

quiz.prompt: By the time you _____ , we will have left. (arrive)
quiz.hint: Careful with the deadline clause itself.
quiz.explain: The clause that sets the deadline stays in the present, even though it describes the future.

quiz.prompt: Next month she _____ here for ten years. (work)
quiz.hint: A total counted up to a future point.
quiz.explain: Counting a total up to a future moment is the future perfect. Will work would only say it happens.

quiz.prompt: Don't ring him now — he _____ by now. (land)
quiz.explain: The future perfect also carries a confident assumption about something already finished: he will have landed by now.

quiz.prompt: They _____ by Monday, so don't expect an answer. (not / decide)
quiz.explain: Won't have + participle. It says the decision is still outstanding when Monday comes.
Questions invert will: Will you have eaten? The participle of eat is eaten, not ate.

quiz.prompt: I _____ at five, so ring me any time after that. (finish)
quiz.hint: Is there a deadline here, or a time?
quiz.explain: At five names when the action happens, not a point to look back from. That is camp seven.

quiz.prompt: I _____ it to you by Friday. (send)
quiz.explain: By Friday is a deadline, so the future perfect: it will already be sent when Friday comes.

quiz.hint: Standing at a future point, looking back.
quiz.explain: Looking back from a future moment takes the future perfect, and the participle of forget is forgotten.

quiz.prompt: By the end of the tour the band _____ in twelve countries. (play)
quiz.explain: A running total counted up to a future point is the future perfect.

quiz.prompt: We _____ here until Friday, then we move on. (work)
quiz.explain: Until marks a stretch continuing up to a point, so the future continuous fits. By would have made it a deadline.

quiz.prompt: How much _____ it _____ by the time it's built? (cost)
quiz.hint: A wh- question with a deadline.
quiz.explain: By the time sets the deadline, so the question takes the future perfect. Cost is the same in all three forms.

quiz.prompt: She _____ the keys before you get there. (leave)
quiz.hint: Before also sets a point to look back from.
quiz.explain: Before you get there is a deadline, so the action is already behind you: will have left.

results: Clean run. You can hear a deadline from a time of day, and you keep the by-the-time clause in the present.
Solid progress. Worth a look back at camp seven before camp thirteen.
Good first attempt. The by/until distinction is the part to read again.
